title: Bankruptcy Administration Improvement Act of 2025
official_title: To amend titles 11 and 28, United States Code, to modify the compensation payable to trustees serving in cases under chapter 7 of title 11, United States Code, to extend the term of certain temporary offices of bankruptcy judges, and for other purposes.
likelihoodReason: Enacted as Public Law 119-76 on February 6, 2026. Introduced by Sen. Chris Coons (D-DE) with 3 cosponsors; its trustee-pay increase is funded entirely by bankruptcy-system fees rather than taxpayer appropriations, which limited cost objections, and it cleared both chambers before being signed.
summary: Raises the pay of Chapter 7 bankruptcy trustees, who administer most consumer bankruptcies, from $60 to $120 per case, and pays for it by raising bankruptcy fees. It also extends the terms of several temporary bankruptcy judgeships from 5 to 10 years.
brief: Doubles per-case Chapter 7 trustee compensation to $120, funded by higher bankruptcy fees, and extends temporary bankruptcy judgeships to 10-year terms.

top_lines.headline: Trustee Compensation
subs: Per-case Chapter 7 trustee pay raised from $60 to $120
Base statutory payment raised from $45 to $105 (plus the existing $15)
Applies to cases filed on or after the first October 1 after enactment

top_lines.headline: Bankruptcy Fees and Fund Allocation
subs: Quarterly-fee lookback extended from 5 years to 10 years
Upper quarterly-fee rate raised from 0.8% to 0.9% of disbursements
$5.4M of fees redirected to the general Treasury each year, FY2026-2031

top_lines.headline: Temporary Bankruptcy Judgeships
subs: Terms of specified temporary judgeships extended from 5 to 10 years
Covers judgeships under the 2020 and 2017 bankruptcy judgeship acts

items.main: Names the Act the “Bankruptcy Administration Improvement Act of 2025”.
items.detail: Short-title section — citation name only; no substantive effect.

items.main: States congressional findings that the bankruptcy system is meant to be self-funded, and that chapter 7 trustee pay has stayed at $60 per case since 1994 (a $45 component under 330(b)(1) plus a $15 component under 330(b)(2)).
items.detail: Findings note the $60 paid in 1994 would equal over $125 today by Consumer Price Index estimates; this Act raises total trustee compensation to $120 per case and will not alter the chapter 7 filing fee or the courts' authority to waive fees for indigent individuals. No substantive effect.

items.main: Raises the base statutory compensation for Chapter 7 trustees under 11 U.S.C. 330(b)(1) from $45 to $105 per case, bringing total per-case compensation to $120.
items.detail: The findings state that trustee pay had stayed at $60 per case (a $45 component plus a $15 component) since 1994. The bill strikes subsection 330(e) and reallocates the remainder of fees collected under 28 U.S.C. 1930(a)(1)(A): $63.51 to the section 1931 Treasury fund, $25.00 to a Deficit Reduction Act of 2005 fund, and $51.49 to the United States Trustee System Fund. The United States Trustee System Fund deposit formula in 28 U.S.C. 589a is changed from "40.46 percent of the fees collected" to a flat "$51.49 of the fees collected in each case."

items.main: Adjusts the Chapter 11 quarterly fee structure and redirects $5.4M of collected fees per year to the general Treasury through fiscal year 2031.
items.detail: The quarterly-fee measurement period in 28 U.S.C. 1930(a)(6)(B) is extended from 5 years to 10 years, the upper rate is raised from 0.8 percent to 0.9 percent of disbursements, and a "greater of" floor is added to the 0.4 percent alternative. For each of fiscal years 2026 through 2031, $5.4M of the quarterly fees collected is deposited in the general fund of the Treasury, with the remainder deposited as specified in section 589a(f).

sections.label: Section 5 — Extension of Temporary Bankruptcy Judgeships

items.main: Extends the terms of certain temporary bankruptcy judge offices from 5 years to 10 years.
items.detail: The change applies to temporary judgeships authorized under Section 4 of the Bankruptcy Administration Improvement Act of 2020 and Section 1003(b)(2)(A) of the Bankruptcy Judgeship Act of 2017, each amended to replace "5 years" with "10 years."

sections.label: Section 6 — Effective Date; Application of Amendments

items.main: Sets the Act's amendments to take effect on the first day of the calendar quarter on or after enactment, with exceptions for Sections 3 and 4.
items.detail: Section 3 (trustee compensation) applies to chapter 7 cases (or chapter 11/12/13 cases converted to chapter 7) commenced on or after the October 1 first occurring after enactment; Section 4 (bankruptcy fees) applies to chapter 11 cases pending on the first calendar quarter on or after enactment and to quarterly fees for disbursements in any quarter beginning on or after enactment.

underreported.section: Section 4(c) — fees diverted to the general fund
underreported.summary: For each of fiscal years 2026 through 2031, $5.4M of the quarterly fees collected is deposited into the general fund of the Treasury rather than the bankruptcy-system funds.
underreported.why_unreported: The bill is framed around keeping the bankruptcy system self-funding, but this provision routes a fixed slice of fee revenue to the general Treasury, away from the trustee and court funds the other provisions support.

underreported.summary: The bill strikes subsection (e) of 11 U.S.C. 330 in the course of raising trustee pay.
underreported.why_unreported: The compensation increase is the headline, but it is paired with the removal of an existing subsection of the trustee-compensation statute.

gaps: The findings note trustees receive no compensation for cases in which the filing fee is waived, but the bill does not provide compensation for those waived-fee cases.
The bill raises per-case trustee pay to $120 but does not index that amount for future inflation, the same gap the findings identify with the 1994 figure.

added: Adds a fixed $5.4M annual deposit of bankruptcy fees to the general Treasury for fiscal years 2026-2031
modified: Chapter 7 trustee base compensation raised from $45 to $105 per case (11 U.S.C. 330(b)(1))
Chapter 11 upper quarterly-fee rate raised from 0.8% to 0.9% of disbursements (28 U.S.C. 1930(a)(6)(B))
Quarterly-fee measurement period extended from 5 years to 10 years
Terms of specified temporary bankruptcy judgeships extended from 5 years to 10 years

featured_quotes.name: Mr. Cline
featured_quotes.text: again, this important legislation promotes efficient government rather than expanding it, reinforces user-funded government services, strengthens accountability and oversight, and reduces market distortions caused by uncertainty.
